clue.text: Reveals how to struggle free from frenzied wolfhounds

indicators.note: struggling free from something means getting out of it, so the letters of how come out of the jumble
frenzied dogs are wild and disordered, so the letters of wolfhounds are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice on escaping a pack of maddened Irish hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'frenzied' scrambles WOLFHOUNDS, and 'to struggle free from' takes the letters H, O, W out of the mix; what is left rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfold a story or plan is to disclose it gradually, so the verb is a synonym of reveals.

clue.text: Selection of panda food will, it's said, confound

indicators.note: it's said tells us the answer is how the preceding words sound when spoken

parts.note: pandas eat bamboo, so a selection of their food is BAMBOOS, and will contracts to 'LL

explanation.surface: A claim that some of a panda's food will puzzle you.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'bamboos'll' (bamboos will) out loud and it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bamboozle someone is to trick or baffle them, a close synonym of confound.

clue.text: Ominously, it appears the singer's suffering upset stomach

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle of the phrase, and suffering it upset means that central pair is turned round

parts.note: a singer is an informer, someone who sings to the police; THE RAT is such a person

explanation.surface: Someone notices a vocalist ominously sick with a bad tummy.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle pair ER of THE RAT is reversed, giving RE. The definition is cryptic: a threat is something that appears ominously.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a looming sign of danger, the thing that shows up as a menace or warning.

clue.text: Reassembly of features page recently stolen from computer department

parts.note: stolen goods still being hot means they were recently taken
OF IT: of means from, and IT is the information technology or computer department

explanation.surface: A page went missing from the IT office, its features reassembled.
explanation.definitionFit: A Photofit is a picture of a suspect's face built up from separate stock facial pieces.

clue.text: Bottled Pils design's what causes ruin

indicators.note: bottled is slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A lager-label design blamed for causing someone's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottled' is the anagram signal; the fodder uses the S of 'design's', so 'causes' links fodder to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to pigs and whistles is an old Scottish idiom for going to wreck, so the phrase names utter destruction.

clue.text: $1,000 splits typical of Orange contract

indicators.note: splits means one piece breaks the other apart by sitting inside it

parts.note: an orange is the textbook example of an oblate shape, a sphere flattened at the poles
I for one plus G for a grand, slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A thousand-dollar cut of a mobile network's typical deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads Orange as the phone company, but here it is the fruit whose shape is oblate.
explanation.definitionFit: To obligate is to bind someone by a duty, as a contract does, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Helpful to have the real reason for Fawkes's failure?

definitions.meaning: being ... means being useful or helpful

definitions.text: the real reason for Fawkes's failure?
definitions.meaning: Guy Fawkes's gunpowder plot failed with no fuse ever lit

explanation.surface: A wry claim to know why the Gunpowder Plot fizzled.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes was caught in 1605 guarding gunpowder under Parliament before it was lit; splitting the answer 1,4 as O FUSE gives the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Of use is an idiom for serving a purpose, so it matches helpful.

clue.text: Endless profession of pulpiteer, laying it on with a trowel?

definitions.text: laying it on with a trowel?

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a preacher in the pulpit would profess 'I'm pastor'

explanation.surface: A preacher's never-ending sermon, flattering his flock too heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laying it on with a trowel' usually means overdoing flattery; here it is literal painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is a painting technique in which paint is applied very thickly, often with a palette knife.

clue.text: Round closing time, Arkwright's not — we trust — purveying pork pies!

definitions.text: not — we trust — purveying pork pies

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: closing means wrapping around, so one piece shuts in the other

parts.note: Noah built the ark, making him a cryptic ark-wright

explanation.surface: Arkwright, the shopkeeper of Open All Hours, at closing time, is hopefully telling no fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pork pies' is rhyming slang for lies. Arkwright suggests the sitcom shopkeeper, but here it is a builder of an ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking on oath means sworn to tell the truth, so not telling lies, we hope.

clue.text: Stick around Tom, Dick and Harry, pub bound!

indicators.note: around tells us the first piece goes about the second

parts.note: gum is a glue, so to gum is to stick
Tom, Dick and Harry means everybody, ALL
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: Everyday chaps glued together heading for the boozer.
explanation.definitionFit: To galumph is to move with clumsy leaps, a heavy kind of bounding.

clue.text: Producers of tittle-tattle from story of roofer's partner with hose?

definitions.note: the garment worn as a pair with hose; singular in the clue, plural in the answer

indicators.note: producers of means the answer names whatever made the following word, here the act of doubling letters
a roofer's story is a TILE TALE, the starting point the doubled letters are added to

parts.note: read as the result of an operation: doubling each T of a roofer's tale makes this word pair

explanation.surface: The source of gossip about a roofer's mate in tights.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as DOUBLE TS: doubling the Ts of TILE TALE gives TITTLE TATTLE. The 's of roofer's links the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet was the close-fitting jacket worn together with hose by Tudor men.

clue.text: Musical setting for Mamma Mia!, from the soundtrack?

indicators.note: a soundtrack is heard, so the answer is what the country's name sounds like

parts.note: the film Mamma Mia! is set on a Greek island, so its setting is Greece

explanation.surface: Asking whether a musical's location makes it a musical itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is the 1971 stage show and 1978 film with John Travolta, a well-known musical.

clue.text: In the end, Lethbridge ordered mass on to new Alberta city

indicators.note: in the end picks the closing letter of each of the two words

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Lethbridge, a city in Alberta, finally ordered a church service moved to another Alberta city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like an anagram signal but only gives its last letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmonton is the provincial capital of Alberta in western Canada.

clue.text: Impressed by delivery date, turn to that man Jack to work

indicators.note: impressed by means pressed into, so the following pieces go inside the date

parts.note: the date of a baby's delivery is a date of birth, DOB

indicators.note: turn tells us the word to is read backwards

parts.note: HE is the pronoun for that man
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A man named Jack is stamped with a delivery date and set to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To do the job is an idiom for being effective, the sense in which a remedy works.

clue.text: Clue deciphered about a central cluster of Egyptian trees

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the a
deciphering a clue means working it out, so its letters are reordered
a central cluster is the four letters at the heart of the word

explanation.surface: A solver cracks a clue about Egyptian trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deciphered' marks the anagram that sits around A, giving EUCAL; 'central cluster of' takes the middle four letters of Egyptian.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalypti is the Latin plural of eucalyptus, the gum tree of Australia.

clue.text: In the beginning, long one assigned to cat?

definitions.text: In the beginning, long one assigned to cat?

indicators.note: in the beginning takes only the opening letter of long

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: A cat is given one of its nine lives, a long one, at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a playful definition: a cat starts with nine lives, and each life is a line it is assigned.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeline is a means of rescue or support, and a cat's spare lives work as that.

clue.text: Alongside this female comedian — what about that?

parts.note: HER is the female pronoun

indicators.note: about means the exclamation wraps around the comedian

parts.note: EH is an exclamation meaning what?
a wit is a clever comic

explanation.surface: Someone says they're enclosing this funny woman, and asks what you think of that.
explanation.definitionFit: Herewith is formal letter-writing for enclosed with this, as in documents sent with a letter.

clue.text: In which we may see pride in the end go before a fall?

definitions.text: In which we may see pride in the end go before a fall?

indicators.note: in the end means only the final letter of pride is used

parts.note: a trip is a stumble and fall

explanation.surface: A spin on the proverb that pride goes before a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an ego trip is a display of pride, and the proverb says one ends in a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is self-indulgent behaviour that feeds one's vanity, in other words a show of pride.

clue.text: More than two or three unwanted publicity cuts withdrawn

indicators.note: cuts means the publicity piece slices into the other word

parts.note: someone withdrawn is aloof, distant and reserved
AD is an advertisement, publicity the reader did not ask for

explanation.surface: Several cuts withdrawn because of bad press.
explanation.definitionFit: A load of is an informal quantity phrase meaning many, so plenty more than a couple.

clue.text: Uniform is black trousers, ready to supply

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the black piece pockets the uniform letter

parts.note: sable is the heraldic word for black
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A dress code: the uniform is black trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like part of a uniform but is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Something issuable can be issued or handed out, so it is available to be supplied.

clue.text: Exclusive series of Peterhouse lectures

indicators.note: series of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grand-sounding run of talks at Peterhouse, a Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: A select club or group is exclusive, open only to a chosen few.

clue.text: Band starts off very quickly on radio cover

indicators.note: the outer letters cover the answer, which sits hidden between them

parts.words: starts off very quickly on radio
parts.note: the starts of very and quickly are V and Q, said on radio as Victor and Quebec

explanation.surface: A band begins its radio set at a gallop and then plays a cover version.
explanation.walkthrough: In radio codes V is VICTOR and Q is QUEBEC; the answer is concealed across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A torque is a twisted metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts, a band of gold or bronze.

clue.text: Rockers playing piece that's powerful

definitions.meaning: ... were a famous British rock band
the most powerful piece in chess

explanation.definitionFit: Queen is both the band of Freddie Mercury and the strongest piece on a chessboard.

clue.text: Lots of people cycling after high scorer?

indicators.note: after says the crowd piece comes after the height piece

parts.note: tall means high

indicators.note: cycling means letters move round from one end to the other

parts.note: many means lots of people

explanation.surface: A cycling crowd behind the top points scorer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tallyman keeps a tally, a running count, so he is literally one who keeps score.

clue.text: Volition's something that may get Spooner a little ruffled?

indicators.note: Spooner is the clergyman who swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds are exchanged

parts.note: wee is Scots for little
a frill is a ruffle of gathered cloth

explanation.surface: A question of whether choice can leave you slightly flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Free will is the power of choosing for oneself, the same thing as volition.

clue.text: Attractive scabbards for old blade

indicators.note: a scabbard sheathes a sword, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: cute means attractive
to can mean for, as in a toast to someone

explanation.surface: Pretty sheaths designed for an antique sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuttoe is an archaic word for a large knife or sword, so an old blade.

clue.text: Sizable pasta slices, second being free?

indicators.note: the pasta slices into the size, sitting in its middle

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing label for large sizes
penne is a tube-shaped pasta

explanation.surface: Large chunks of pasta, one portion free of charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Openness is the state of being frank or unrestricted, the condition of being free and open.
